lesson.title: Busca el Color: A Classroom Color Hunt
lesson.subject: spanish

contentBlocks.text: Sol wants to play a hunting game today — but instead of hidden cards, we're hunting for colors that are already all around the room!
When Sol calls a color, touch something that color as fast as you can! Sol says '¡rojo!' — run and touch something red. '¡azul!' — touch something blue. '¡verde!' — touch something green.
Now Sol calls the trickier colors: '¡amarillo!' — touch something yellow. '¡blanco!' — touch something white. '¡negro!' — touch something black. Listen closely, because Sol mixes them all up!
You hunted down every color Sol called — rojo, azul, amarillo, verde, blanco, negro — all around the room! Tomorrow, Sol has a colorful story to share.

config.instructions: Match the Spanish color word to its color.

objectives: Touch an object of the correct color when they hear a Spanish color word
Recognize all six color words — rojo, azul, amarillo, verde, blanco, negro — spoken out of song order
materialsNeeded: A room or space with objects in many colors (toys, books, clothing, furniture)
teacherGuide.facilitationScript:
1. Stand with Sol in the middle of the room and explain that today's hunt is for colors that are already all around you.
2. Have Sol call a color in Spanish — start with rojo, azul, verde — and model running to touch something that color yourself.
3. Have your child listen for each color and touch a matching object; celebrate every correct find.
4. Add the trickier colors — amarillo, blanco, negro — and call all six in a mixed-up order so your child is truly listening.
5. Swap roles: let your child call a color for you or Sol to find.
6. Complete the on-screen matching activity together, reading each color word aloud since your child may not read yet.
7. Close by asking: 'Which color was the hardest to find in this room?'
differentiationTips: Struggling: call only rojo, azul, and amarillo, and point toward the right area of the room if your child is stuck
Ready for more: call two colors in a row for your child to touch in order, or ask for a second object of the same color
A near-miss — touching blue when you said green — is a normal listening slip; name the color again and move on
teacherGuide.answerKey: This is a spoken listening-and-hunting activity — success looks like your child touching an object of the right color after hearing each word, not a written answer. In the matching game: rojo → red, azul → blue, amarillo → yellow, verde → green, blanco → white, negro → black.
teacherGuide.standardsRationale: Deepens week 5's WA-WL-2015.1.2 target by moving from the predictable song order into a mixed-order listening game where the child has to identify each color word cold and respond physically — real comprehension rather than memorized sequence — and the on-screen matching activity gives the same six-color recognition a quiet digital rep.

worksheet.title: Busca el Color: A Classroom Color Hunt

generationData.instructions: Read each line aloud to your child and do the action together.

rows.problem: Stand together in a room with lots of different-colored objects.
Call a color in Spanish — rojo, azul, verde — and touch something that color together.
Add amarillo, blanco, and negro, calling all six colors in a mixed-up order to hunt for.
